label: early copy steps (2nd/3rd output) of long sequences, when the fed-back token is e/s/h/r/w/z/x/l/b
explanation: Active only in the copy phase (never during original tokens or on <DEL>). Concentrated at absolute steps t=10-11, which for long sequences are the 2nd/3rd outputs (recall_idx 1-2; L=9 gives 82% of the mass, L=8 15%; L<=5 essentially never). A smaller secondary bump sits at the last two steps of L=9 sequences (t=16-17, ~13% of mass). Within those positions it depends strongly on the fed-back input token (the copy of orig(0)/orig(1)): e, s, h, r give 3.6-5.5x lift, w/z/x/l/b about 1.5-2.3x; most other letters and digits rarely trigger it. Strongest activations (top examples) are at recall_idx 1-2 of L=9 sequences beginning with e/s/w/h. Precision is incomplete because the token preference is graded rather than a clean set, and recall misses the late-sequence bump and weaker scattered copy-phase firings. Dev F1 0.53, mass recall 0.68.
